functional.text: A user uploads a photo with a caption; followers see it once it is processed.
A user scrolls a home feed of photos from accounts they follow, 10 per page.
Follow / unfollow accounts; profiles show follower and following counts.
Like / unlike a photo; every photo shows its like count and whether I liked it.

non_functional.text: Feed p99 < 500 ms; images load from a nearby edge; read-heavy (~50 feed loads per upload).
A processed photo reaches followers' feeds within ~5 s.
Durability: an acknowledged upload is never lost (replicated across zones, 11 nines).
Like counts may lag by a few seconds, but my own like shows immediately and is counted once.

assumptions.text: 500M DAU; 100M uploads/day; 10 feed opens and 8 likes per user per day; peak = 2–2.5× average.
Original ~2 MB; four renditions add ~0.5 MB.
~150 followers on average; a few accounts have hundreds of millions.

out_of_scope.text: Video and stories, direct messages, comments, search, ads.

api.notes: The app PUTs the photo bytes straight to object storage through the CDN edge.
Idempotency-Key header; becomes visible when renditions are ready.

data.name: posts
data.fields: post_id (PK, time-sortable), author_id, caption, media_keys, status, created_at
data.why: Photo metadata read by id in batches; bytes live in object storage.

data.name: follow graph
data.why: Two adjacency lists partitioned by user: each direction is one range scan.

data.name: likes
data.why: Source of truth for 'liked by me' and for rebuilding counters.

data.name: like_counters
data.why: Batched increments; hot posts split across sub-keys.

deep_dives.title: Double taps and retries: counting each like once

options.name: Count every like request
options.cons: retries and double taps inflate counts

options.name: Unique (post_id, user_id) row; emit an event only when the insert succeeds; aggregator dedups by event id
options.pros: each like counted once end to end
options.cons: one extra conditional write per like

deep_dives.choice: Insert-if-absent on (post_id, user_id), emit +1 only on success, dedup events by id in the aggregator
deep_dives.why: The stream is at-least-once, so the aggregator must be idempotent too; the likes row makes 'liked by me' exact even while the count lags.

deep_dives.title: Renditions: eager or on demand

options.name: Eager: make every size right after upload
options.pros: first view is fast; CDN warm
options.cons: CPU and storage for sizes nobody requests

options.name: On demand: resize on first CDN miss
options.cons: first viewer waits; thundering herd on a viral miss

deep_dives.choice: Eager for the 3–4 sizes the app uses (WebP/AVIF), on demand for rare ones
deep_dives.why: Feed sizes are requested almost immediately by followers, so eager work is never wasted; rare sizes would cost storage on 100M photos a day.

wrapup.bottlenecks: Hot like counters on viral posts (sub-key sharding, batched increments), fan-out for huge accounts (pull them instead), resize queue backlog after spikes (autoscale workers on queue depth), CDN origin load (origin shield).
wrapup.failures: Uploads are durable before ack (multi-zone object storage); resize jobs retry from the queue and are idempotent per media_id; counters rebuild from the likes table; a lost feed-cache shard is rebuilt by pulling; stuck 'processing' posts are swept and retried.
wrapup.monitoring: Upload success rate, upload → visible latency, resize queue depth, feed p99, CDN hit ratio, counter lag, orphaned uploads.
wrapup.scale: Shard posts, graph and likes by id; add fan-out workers and queue partitions; tier old originals to colder storage classes; push renditions to more edge locations.
wrapup.future: Video and stories (transcoding ladders), comments, search and explore, an ML-ranked feed.

parts.title: Media upload pipeline
parts.problem: Take in ~1.2k photo uploads/s (peak ~3k) of ~2 MB each, keep them durable, produce resized renditions and deliver images worldwide, without streaming ~250 TB/day through the API servers.

options.name: Upload through the API servers, store bytes in the database
options.cons: API servers stream terabytes; the database bloats and backups explode

options.name: Upload through the API servers to object storage, resize inline
options.cons: requests hold connections for seconds; resize CPU sits on the request path

options.name: Presigned PUT straight to object storage; object-created event queues resize jobs; CDN serves renditions
options.pros: servers only sign URLs; processing scales separately; immutable files cache forever
options.cons: two-step publish; orphan uploads need a cleanup job

parts.choice: Presigned direct upload to object storage, asynchronous resize workers fed by object-created events, CDN delivery
parts.why: ~250 TB/day of bytes never touch the services; resize workers autoscale on queue depth; renditions are immutable so the CDN hit ratio is very high, which keeps N1 for images.

parts.title: Follow graph
parts.problem: Answer 'all followers of X' when distributing a post and 'who X follows' for the feed and profile, for ~150 follows on average and up to 300M followers on one account.

options.name: One SQL follows table with two indexes
options.cons: one table with ~75B rows; followers-of a celebrity is a huge index scan on one shard

options.name: Two denormalized adjacency lists in a wide-column store, partitioned by user
options.pros: each direction is a single-partition range scan; scales horizontally
options.cons: two writes per follow; repair job for drift

options.name: Graph database
options.cons: we only need one hop; harder to shard and operate

parts.choice: Two adjacency lists (followers-of, following-of) in a wide-column store, counts and celebrity flags cached
parts.why: Both queries are one-hop lookups by user, so partitioning by user makes each a single range scan; huge follower lists are paged by the fan-out workers or skipped for celebrities.

parts.title: Feed generation
parts.problem: Serve ~116k feed pages/s at peak in < 500 ms; decide whether a user's feed is assembled at read time or prepared when a photo becomes ready.

options.name: Pull: query every followee's recent posts on open
Push: write each new post id into every follower's feed
options.pros: a load is one cache read
options.cons: ~175k inserts/s and 300M inserts for one celebrity post

options.name: Hybrid push + pull for huge accounts, ranked over candidates
options.pros: cheap reads, bounded writes, room for ranking
options.cons: two code paths; merge at read time

parts.choice: Hybrid fan-out triggered by 'post ready' events; huge accounts merged at read time; a lightweight ranker orders the candidates
parts.why: Reads dominate (≈ 50 feed loads per upload), so precompute; triggering on 'post ready' means followers never see a photo without renditions; skipping accounts above ~1M followers bounds the write cost.

parts.title: Likes and counters
parts.problem: Record ~46k likes/s (peak ~100k), one per user per photo, and show like counts on every feed item, when a viral photo can take thousands of likes per second on one counter.

options.name: UPDATE posts SET likes = likes + 1 per like
options.cons: row-lock contention on hot posts; a write on the post row per like

options.name: Redis INCR per like
options.cons: one hot key per viral post; drifts from the source of truth after failures

options.name: Idempotent likes rows + like events on a stream + batched aggregation into sharded counters
options.pros: hot posts become a few batched writes; counts rebuildable

parts.choice: Likes rows with insert-if-absent, +1/-1 events on a stream, an aggregator applying batched +n to counters split into sub-keys for hot posts
parts.why: N4 allows seconds of lag on counts; batching turns thousands of increments on one post into a few writes; the likes table stays the source of truth for 'liked by me' and for rebuilding counters.
